title: Hate Radio by Milo Rau at St Ann’s Warehouse #hateradio #milorau #sta...
transcript: Violence is almost mundane in the absolutely chilling Hate Radio by Milo Rau. As a historical documentary piece, it's primarily a recreation of a radio broadcast that preceded the 1994 Rwandan genocide. The hosts play music, they joke, interact with listeners, and gleefully celebrate the extermination of the Tutsi minority who they refer to as “cockroaches.” The dissonance between the gleeful atmosphere and what they're preaching is stunning. And although this piece first premiered in 2011, it feels remarkably timely. American audiences will easily draw a connection between these hosts and modern day podcasters who propagandize and weaponize our propensity toward hate and division. In nontraditional fashion for a theatre piece, you listen to the show through headphones, making the delivery of the broadcast feel especially direct. Experiencing it this way made me consider how malleable we are in isolation — how much we're shaped by the media we consume, whether we realize it or not. It's a tough one, but I found it very insightful. Hate Radio is running now at St Ann’s Warehouse. With that, another program for my collection.
